S4.description:
Rebuild after restart does not create a second commitment for one effect

risk: retry_safety (priority P0)
purpose: Exercise 'rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect': after a restart (state re-derived from durable history), confirm the ledger still holds at most one live-or-committed grant per (tenant, commit_key) and at most one CLAIMED grant per effect.
requirement: U-P5-1: rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect
product principle: outcome_verification
rationale: Re-executing an effect on rebuild would surface as a duplicate live/CLAIMED grant for the same commit_key; the live-hold and commit-once uniqueness are exactly the durable guards this AC leans on.

S5.name: generated:S5
S5.description:
Witness-to-grant stays 1:1 across a restart-driven rebuild

risk: safety_invariant (priority P1)
purpose: Exercise 'rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect' from the witness side: after restart, every checkpoint-minted grant has exactly one witness and no grant has two witnesses, so a replay cannot fabricate a second authorized effect.
requirement: U-P5-1: rebuilding state from history never re-executes an effect
product principle: outcome_verification
rationale: The kernel's contract is witness:grant = 1:1; a rebuild that duplicated or dropped a witness would either re-authorize or orphan an effect, both violations of the AC.
